indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B2.5.3.1: Recognize the impact of science and technology in society
indicator.objective: Identify the technological devices used in the community and describe their impact

skills.description: Identify technological devices used in the community
Describe the impact of technology on society
Compare how things were done in the past without technology
Draw a technological device and describe how it helps the community

misconceptions: Technology only means mobile phones and computers.
Life was exactly the same before these technologies were invented.
Technology has no effect on how people live.
A sewing machine or a car is not technology.
Technology can solve every problem without any human effort.

questions.stem: Which of these is a technological device used in the community?
questions.explanation: A mobile phone is a technological device used for communication in the community.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think natural things are technology.

questions.stem: Which of these technologies helps people travel from one town to another?
questions.explanation: A car is a technology used for transportation.
questions.misconception: Pupils may name household items instead of transport.

questions.stem: How does a mobile phone help people?
options: It helps them talk to people far away
hints: You can talk to someone in another town.
questions.explanation: A mobile phone helps people communicate with others who are far away.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think phones have physical abilities.

questions.stem: How did people send messages to far places before mobile phones were invented?
options: By sending letters through the post
hints: It took a long time to arrive.
questions.explanation: Before phones, people sent letters by post, which took much longer.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think people always had phones.

questions.stem: Which of these is a technology used in hospitals?
questions.explanation: A thermometer is a technological device used in hospitals to check body temperature.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not think of medical tools as technology.

questions.stem: How has technology helped farmers?
options: By providing tools like tractors to farm faster
By making crops grow without water
By making the sun shine at night
hints: Think about machines on a farm.
It helps them do work faster.
questions.explanation: Technology has helped farmers by providing tools like tractors that make farming faster and easier.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think technology controls the weather.

questions.stem: How has technology helped doctors and nurses in hospitals?
options: By providing machines to check and treat sick people
By making sick people run faster
By making medicine taste like sweets
hints: Doctors use machines to help patients.
questions.explanation: Technology has helped doctors and nurses by providing medical machines and tools to check and treat patients.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not understand the medical applications of technology.

questions.stem: How did people travel long distances before cars and buses were invented?
options: By walking or using animals like horses
hints: What did people use before engines?
They used their feet or animals.
questions.explanation: Before cars and buses, people walked or used animals like horses and donkeys for long journeys.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think modern transport always existed.

questions.stem: Which of these is a technological device used in a market?
hints: Traders use it to sell food.
questions.explanation: A weighing scale is a technological device used in markets to measure the weight of goods.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not think of simple tools as technology.

questions.stem: What impact has the mobile phone had on how people do business in Ghana?
options: Traders can call customers and arrange deliveries easily
Traders can no longer sell goods
Traders have to walk to every customer
hints: They can call or send mobile money.
questions.explanation: Mobile phones allow traders to communicate quickly with customers, arrange deliveries, and even receive payments through mobile money, making business easier.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not see the business impact of phones.

questions.stem: Name one technological device used in your community.
hints: What helps people communicate or travel?
questions.explanation: Common devices include mobile phones, cars, radios, and televisions.

questions.stem: Name one way a mobile phone has changed how people live.
answer: we can talk to people far away
hints: How do you contact your friends?
questions.explanation: Mobile phones have changed how we live by allowing us to communicate easily, send money, and access information.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not see the impact of phones beyond playing games.

questions.stem: How has technology changed the way people get water in many communities?
options: People can use boreholes and pumps instead of walking to rivers
People use stones to get water
questions.explanation: Technology like boreholes and pumps has made it easier to get clean water without walking long distances to rivers.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not connect water access to technology.

questions.stem: Ama says 'Technology only means mobile phones and computers.' Is she right?
options: No, things like cars and radios are also technology
Yes, only phones and computers are technology
hints: Is a car made by people to help us?
questions.explanation: Technology includes any tool or machine made by people to help us, not just phones and computers.
questions.misconception: Pupils often limit technology to digital devices.

questions.stem: How did people preserve food before refrigerators were invented?
options: By drying, smoking, or salting it
By putting it in the freezer
By using ice blocks from shops
hints: The sun and fire were used.
questions.explanation: Before fridges, people preserved food by drying it in the sun, smoking it over a fire, or salting it.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think people always had fridges.

questions.stem: What is one negative impact of technology on the environment?
questions.explanation: Technology can cause pollution from factories, cars, and electronic waste, which harms the environment.
questions.misconception: Pupils may only see the positive side of technology.

questions.stem: Draw one technological device used in your community. Write a sentence to describe how it helps people.

criteria.description: Writes a correct description of how it helps

hints: Think of a car or a phone.
questions.explanation: This tests identification of technology and its impact.

questions.stem: Explain how technology has changed the way people communicate in Ghana over the past 50 years.

criteria.description: States that people used to send letters, which took a long time
States that people now use mobile phones to call, text, and use the internet instantly

hints: How did people communicate before phones?
questions.explanation: In the past, people relied on letters that took days or weeks. Now, mobile phones allow instant communication across the country and the world.

questions.stem: Write down one positive and one negative impact of technology on society.

criteria.description: States a positive impact (e.g., faster communication, easier travel)
States a negative impact (e.g., pollution, job loss)

questions.explanation: Positive: faster communication. Negative: pollution from factories and cars.

questions.stem: Tell your teacher about one technological device you use at home and explain how it has changed your life.

criteria.description: Explains how it has changed their life

hints: Think about your phone or TV.
What can you do now that you couldn't before?
questions.explanation: This tests the ability to identify technology and its personal impact.
